lines: A pan of oil is on fire. Never pour water on it!
Water is heavier than oil, so it sinks straight to the bottom.
The oil is over one hundred ninety degrees. The water flashes to steam.
Steam takes up seventeen hundred times more room.
It blasts burning oil everywhere. A fireball can reach the ceiling.
Myth: a tiny splash is fine. Nope. Even a splash can erupt.
Instead, turn off the heat and slide a metal lid on top.
No air, no fire. Keep the lid on until it's cool.
Tiny fire? Baking soda works. Flour just burns.
Spreading? Get out and call emergency services.
So what's your first move, water or lid?
The lid. Starve it of air.
